item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded:
Incidentally, from what I've read, there is a group that destroys SCP-type objects whenever it can - the GOC. They would certainly destroy this ASAP.

The Foundation, however, is not the GOC. The Foundation contains things, out of either a "Might find a use for this someday" mentality, a "Don't break what you can't fix" mentality, or a "For SCIENCE!" mentality - it only destroys them when it has to. The GOC holds the Foundation in contempt precisely because it doesn't just destroy things like this.

This is just the impression I get, though.

item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded:
WRONG!

The Foundation is all about containing things that they cannot destroy and have no potential use if they are paranormal or otherwise abberant.

What they are NOT about is coddling them.

item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded:
This organization is run by packrats. The Overseers keep all this junk around for the same reason I have fourteen tabs open and no intent to close any of them.

Yeah, remember, in-universe, the foundation won't bother to contain something that they can destroy and has no potential use. Behind the scenes, we only decommission things that are deemed not up to par writing-wise, and that somebody bothers to write a decommissioning for (anything else is merely deleted :D). Hence despite what the official stance is, they tend to rarely get rid of stuff (I'd assume mostly because they are genuinely curious about what they find, hence the packrattiness).

Their purpose is to safeguard humanity from these things, which often necessitates that some things be destroyed. I can understand them keeping useless shit like the vending machines around for the sake of comic relief, but a statuette that surprises people doesn't seem to have any sort of value that would justify keeping it around. What's the point?

Why would they waste the manpower keeping an eye on it? The room to house it?

Don't get me wrong, I actually like this concept a lot and the article is well written. But you gotta keep in mind the purpose of this organization.

item.content:encoded:
At first, I thought, "Good grief, it's a Lighter And Softer knock-off of SCP-173 and SCP-689."

But when I finished, I thought, "Huh. In spite of the massive similarities … somehow this one works for me."

I guess the non-lethal nature of this one, ironically, makes it scarier. If 173 or 689 catch you, you'll be dead before it ever occurs to you to be afraid. This one? You're walking along, for some reason you turn around, an-OHHOLYSHITITSRIGHTBEHINDYOU! My little brother and I used to try to do things like that to each other all the time, usually by hiding in the bathroom, just next to the door.
